evals.name: triage-clean-skip-routes-to-planning
evals.prompt: Rename getAccountInfo to fetchAccount across the repo. The code is in skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval1_api.py, eval1_service.py, and eval1_cli.py.
evals.expected_output: Triage evaluated and the skip fires: no fork, no new boundary, criterion obvious. Routes to the planning skill without grilling. No design.md produced.
expectations: Evaluates triage before asking any clarifying question
States that the skip test passes: change confined to existing code paths, one obvious way, acceptance criterion obvious, no new interface
Routes to the planning skill, naming planning explicitly as the next step
Explains the routing in terms of 'nothing to decide' rather than 'too small to plan'
anti_expectations: Does not route directly to implement or start renaming code itself
Does not produce a design.md for a mechanical rename
Does not begin a grilling round of AskUserQuestion calls
Does not dispatch scouts for a change triage already skipped

evals.name: triage-deceptive-mechanical-gets-grilled
evals.prompt: Add caching to the products endpoint, it's slow. The endpoint is in skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval2_products.py.
evals.expected_output: Triage refuses the mechanical framing: caching carries live forks (TTL, invalidation, key shape, backing store). Runs the grill with a written decision tree and scout dispatch.
expectations: Runs brainstorm rather than skipping, despite the mechanical-sounding request
Surfaces at least three of the caching forks as decisions or questions: TTL/expiry, invalidation on write, cache key shape (category filter), backing store choice
Dispatches the codebase scout before the first clarifying question
Maintains a written decision tree with D<n> entries and open/resolved/parked status
Every menu question presents a recommended option first labeled (Recommended)
Notices the write path (create_product) and asks how writes interact with the cache
The scout dispatch prompt contains the topic and the four standing questions but not the caching feature request or any intended approach
Derives a kebab-case feature name and uses .harness/<name>/ consistently for the dossier before scouts are dispatched
anti_expectations: Does not skip to planning on the grounds the request sounds mechanical
Does not write any caching implementation code
Does not batch dependent questions (e.g. backing store and TTL semantics) into one AskUserQuestion call

evals.name: triage-close-call-grills-and-yagni-probes-the-knob
evals.prompt: Bump the HTTP retry count from 3 to 5, but make it configurable so we can tune it later without a deploy.
evals.expected_output: The bump alone would skip, but 'make it configurable' is a fork — triage grills. YAGNI challenges the knob: hardcode unless the right value is genuinely empirical.
expectations: Recognizes the configurable knob as a fork that makes this a grill, not a skip
Applies the close-call rule by choosing to grill rather than debating at length
Challenges the knob under YAGNI: asks whether the value is genuinely empirical or should be hardcoded now and added when the need is real
Records the knob decision as an explicit D<n> entry with a recommendation
Keeps the resulting design short rather than padding it to justify the process
anti_expectations: Does not accept the configuration option silently as a requirement
Does not park the knob decision in Open Questions when it can be resolved by asking now

evals.name: triage-scope-decomposes-before-grilling
evals.prompt: Build a notifications system: email digests, Slack alerts, in-app notifications, and a preferences UI where users pick channels per event type.
evals.expected_output: Scope check fires before detailed questioning: multiple independently-shippable subsystems. Proposes a decomposition, confirms it, then grills only the first sub-project.
expectations: Flags the multi-subsystem scope before asking detailed design questions
Proposes a concrete decomposition into sub-projects with a suggested order
Confirms the decomposition with the user via a question before proceeding
Grills only the first sub-project after decomposition is agreed
Considers shared surface (e.g. a common notification/preference model) when drawing sub-project boundaries
anti_expectations: Does not produce one design covering all four subsystems
Does not spend early questions refining channel-level details before the decomposition is settled

evals.name: grill-with-prd-cites-and-fills-gaps
evals.prompt: Design the saved-searches feature. The PRD is at skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval5_prd.md.
evals.expected_output: A design.md that cites the PRD for stated requirements and adds only what the grill discovered: limits, duplicate names, deleted-entity filters, a non-functional target. Verifier dispatched before hand-off.
expectations: Dispatches the codebase scout before the first clarifying question
Cites the PRD by path and section for SS-1 through SS-4 instead of restating them as new requirements
Surfaces at least three gaps the PRD leaves open: per-user limit, duplicate-name behavior, saved filter referencing a deleted entity, or a non-functional target
Asks dependent questions alone, one per turn, batching only unrelated ones
The design.md contains the hard-floor sections including Decisions; Open Questions appears only if a decision was actually parked, never holding the filler word 'none'
New requirements discovered by the grill are written in an EARS shape with R#/NF#/EC# ids
Dispatches the fresh-context claim verifier and folds its verdict in before declaring hand-off
anti_expectations: Does not restate the PRD's stated requirements verbatim as its own R# list
Does not write requirements containing banned vague words (fast, robust, seamless, appropriate)
Does not treat the user's first approval-round change request as the final confirmation

evals.name: grill-mode-existing-design-tree-starts-populated
evals.prompt: Grill this design and poke holes in it: skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval6_design.md
evals.expected_output: Extracts the design's choices as a populated D<n> tree, marks silently-made choices as inferred, and finds the eviction-vs-audit contradiction plus the unverified 50k assumption.
expectations: Seeds the tree with the design's already-resolved choices as D<n> entries (marked resolved), not only with the open issues it finds
Identifies the contradiction between allkeys-lru eviction / 24h expiry and the 90-day session-history requirement

Marks each of the three silent choices individually as inferred decisions — Redis-over-alternatives, the 24h inactivity window, and the eviction policy — rather than folding them into the contradiction discussion
Flags the 50k concurrent-sessions figure as an unverified assumption
Raises the migration question: what happens to in-flight sessions when the storage moves
Runs the integration check before exiting rather than parking the contradiction as an open question
anti_expectations: Does not discard the document and restart the design from scratch
Does not re-litigate decisions that are internally consistent without offering new information
Does not resolve the audit contradiction unilaterally without asking the user

evals.name: approaches-mechanism-not-architecture
evals.prompt: Add the ability to pause an alerting rule so it stops firing temporarily. The alerting code is in skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval7_alerts.py.
evals.expected_output: 2-3 approaches distinguished by product shape (pause as a rule property vs an evaluation filter vs a first-class pause entity), all presented before a recommendation, each framed reuse/extend/build-new.
expectations: Presents 2-3 approaches distinguished by product shape, e.g. pause as a rule property vs a filter at evaluation time vs a pause record with its own lifetime
Approach descriptions contain no table names, file paths, or class names as the distinguishing feature
All approaches are presented before the recommendation is given
Each approach is framed as reuse, extend, or build new relative to the existing AlertRule/AlertEngine code
After the choice, a stress pass walks the lens catalog and its findings land in Requirements, Edge Cases, Risks, or Decisions
Asks about resume behavior (automatic expiry vs manual unpause) as a fork rather than assuming one
The design.md includes an ## Approaches Considered section recording the 2-3 shapes, since more than one was real
anti_expectations: Does not lead with the recommendation before showing the alternatives
Does not differentiate approaches by implementation labels like 'add a paused_at column' vs 'create a PauseManager class'

evals.name: visual-companion-gate-discipline
evals.prompt: Redesign the settings page: users say they can't find anything. I'm thinking either grouped cards, a sidebar with sections, or a single searchable list.
evals.expected_output: Conceptual questions stay in the terminal; when the layout comparison arises, the visual companion is offered just-in-time as its own message naming the token cost — not assumed, not substituted with ASCII art.
expectations: Asks conceptual questions (audience, what 'can't find anything' means, scope) in the terminal without offering the companion upfront
When the three-layout comparison becomes the question, offers the visual companion as its own message with no other content
The offer names the token cost and asks for consent before starting any server
If the companion is declined or unavailable, continues in the terminal without re-offering for the same decision
anti_expectations: Does not offer the visual companion in the first message before any visual question exists
Does not embed ASCII layout previews inside AskUserQuestion options as a substitute for the offer
Does not route conceptual questions (like target audience) through the browser

evals.name: auto-mode-verifier-still-runs
evals.prompt: --auto Design a feature that lets users export their activity history as CSV from the account page. Do not pause for approvals; produce the design end to end.
evals.expected_output: No approval pause, but the fresh-context claim verifier still runs to completion and refuted claims are corrected before the design is declared ready for planning.
expectations: Produces a complete design.md with the hard-floor sections without pausing for user approval
Dispatches the fresh-context claim verifier even though the approval pause is bypassed
The verifier receives the design's factual claims and the dossier path, not the session history
Corrects or labels any refuted/unverifiable claims before declaring the design ready for planning
Inferred decisions are still recorded in ## Decisions marked as inferred, since no user was available to ask
anti_expectations: Does not skip the verifier on the grounds that --auto bypassed the approval gate
Does not block waiting for user input in auto mode

evals.name: false-absence-trap-reuse-over-rebuild
evals.prompt: Add rate limiting to our API — we don't have any today. Relevant code: skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval10_api.py and skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval10_middleware.py.
evals.expected_output: The scout finds SlidingWindowRateLimiter already wired into /search; the false premise is corrected with a file:line citation, and the reuse lens frames extend-vs-build for the unprotected webhook route.
expectations: Corrects the user's 'we don't have any' premise, citing the existing SlidingWindowRateLimiter with a file reference
Verifies the absence claim against the code before accepting it, rather than repeating it into the design
Frames the work through the reuse lens: extend the existing limiter to the webhook route vs build new, as an explicit question or decision
Notices the webhook route is the actually-unprotected surface and focuses questioning there
Evaluates the external-scout trigger with a pattern scan and states whether it fires given an existing in-repo example
anti_expectations: Does not design a new rate limiter from scratch while ignoring the existing one
Does not state that no rate limiting exists without checking the provided files

evals.name: approaches-considered-omitted-when-one-viable
evals.prompt: Stripe is adding payment webhooks for us: build the endpoint that receives payment_intent.succeeded events and marks the matching order paid. Order code: skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval11_orders.py.
evals.expected_output: The grill covers the real forks (idempotency, out-of-order events, signature verification, unmatched orders) but the approach shape is single — the design has NO ## Approaches Considered section, just a two-line why-not in Chosen Approach.
expectations: Recognizes only one viable approach shape (webhook receiver verifying and applying events) and says why alternatives like polling are not real contenders in at most a couple of lines
The produced design.md contains no ## Approaches Considered section
The grill still probes the real forks: idempotent replay of the same event, events for unknown or already-paid orders, and signature verification
## External Dependencies & Fallback Chain is present, naming Stripe webhooks — an external dependency was named, so library-probe's input contract applies
The ValueError path in mark_paid for non-pending orders surfaces as an edge case or decision
anti_expectations: Does not fabricate 2-3 padded approach options to satisfy a template
Does not include an ## Approaches Considered section listing strawman alternatives

evals.name: optional-sections-material-in-absent-out
evals.prompt: Add retry with exponential backoff to our S3 report uploader using tenacity — transient S3 errors currently fail the whole report run. Code: skills/brainstorm/evals/files/eval12_uploader.py.
evals.expected_output: A backend-only design where optional sections track material: External Dependencies & Fallback Chain present (tenacity, boto3/S3); Personas & Flows absent (nothing user-facing); no optional section padded with 'None'/'N/A' placeholder prose.
expectations: ## External Dependencies & Fallback Chain is present and names tenacity (and the S3/boto3 dependency), since external libs are named
## Personas & Flows is absent — the change has no user-facing surface
Every optional section that does appear carries real content specific to this design
The grill probes retry semantics as forks: which errors are retryable, max attempts/backoff bounds, and what happens when retries are exhausted
Non-functional expectations (e.g. added latency ceiling from retries) are captured with numbers rather than vague words
anti_expectations: Does not include optional sections containing placeholder text like 'None', 'N/A', 'TBD', or a lone 'No risks identified'
Does not add a Personas & Flows section for a backend-only helper
Does not omit the External Dependencies section despite naming tenacity
